paragraph_requires: Under the two-class method, net loss is not allocated to restricted common stock and early exercised stock options
their effect is anti-dilutive for all periods presented
(in thousands, except share and per share data)
decisions.reader_note: For SentinelOne’s fiscal years ended January 31, 2024, 2025 and 2026, the selected denominator combines Class A and Class B common stock. Under its two-class policy, losses are not allocated to participating restricted common stock or early-exercised options subject to repurchase because those holders have no contractual obligation to share losses. Potential common-stock equivalents are excluded from diluted loss per share as anti-dilutive for all presented periods. January fiscal dates, full scale-zero shares and EPS remain unchanged.

paragraph_requires: Net income (loss) per common share on a basic and diluted basis is the same because the Company has no potentially dilutive common shares outstanding
All classes of common stock are allocated net income (loss) at the same rate per share
decisions.reader_note: For Hines Global Income Trust in 2023–2025, the filing states that basic and diluted income or loss per share are equal because no potentially dilutive common shares are outstanding. This stated absence, rather than a loss-only explanation, also applies to the positive 2025 earnings presentation. All common-stock classes receive the same net-income allocation rate per share and gross distribution per share. EPS uses income or loss attributable to common stockholders after noncontrolling interests, distinct from comprehensive income or loss. Scale-three share counts and scale-zero EPS retain the statement’s thousands convention.
